stated_limitation: A conservative circular-shift null attenuates these effects, and only a subset of sessions survives it. This is expected rather than damning... One session (c7bd79c9) shows a strong behavioural bias but weak neural decoding, a reminder that decodability depends on which brain regions each probe happened to sample.

justification.dataset: DANDI 000149 (IBL standardized visual-decision task with fixed block priors) is the canonical dataset for demonstrating a latent decision bias, sampled across four Neuropixels sessions.
justification.handling: Real units/trials tables streamed via LINDI, IBL quality-label plus firing-rate unit selection, spike counts aligned to stimOn within the enforced quiescence window, all correct.
justification.analysis: Cross-validated L2 logistic decoding with both a label-shuffle permutation null and a temporally-matched circular-shift null to guard against slow drift is the appropriate and rigorous method.
justification.correctness: Reported AUCs and p-values reproduce exactly from the committed transcript output, are internally consistent with the figures, and rest on adequate trial counts and sound permutation tests.
justification.figures: Figures are labeled with units and reference nulls, the example session is chosen by effect strength (auc minus null-95), and the behavioral, time-resolved, and null-comparison panels clearly show the effect.
justification.honesty: The README is proportionate and names specific limitations (only a subset survives the circular-shift null; one session shows behavioral bias but weak decoding), but the notebook's opening abstract overstates with 'above both null models, in every session,' which its own output contradicts.
justification.verdict: Core work is sound and largely believable; I would ask for the abstract overstatement to be reconciled with the conclusion and a multiple-comparison note added to the single-unit panel before fully accepting.
